text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.6% today, continuing a sharp six-day rally that has pushed the stock up nearly 8% since late September. The move reflects tightening fundamentals in oil refining: crude prices have climbed to $96 locally and $114 globally amid ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict and Middle East supply threats, refineries are operating at a high 92.5% capacity, and gasoline and diesel inventories remain lean—conditions that widen the profit margin for refiners who turn crude into finished fuels.

The broader backdrop is a squeeze on global oil stockpiles that Saudi Aramco's CEO said could take up to two years to resolve, even as the G7 has begun releasing 100 million barrels of reserves to ease pressure. With tankers continuing to face strikes near Iran and military tensions still elevated, the market is pricing in sustained tight supply and strong refining margins ahead.
